summary: This note summarizes World Series championship records by Major League Baseball franchise, listing each team's series appearances and titles in the American and National Leagues. It also gives league-level totals, such as American League teams winning 65 of 113 series, and shares of titles held by the New York Yankees and St. Louis Cardinals. A header section lists the first and most recent years played, current champions and runners-up, and the most titles. The text is partly duplicated, and the Dodgers' appearance count differs between copies (19 and 18).
one_line: Franchise-by-franchise records of World Series appearances and titles, with league totals and current champion details.
key_facts: The New York Yankees played in 40 World Series in the American League and won 27.
The Philadelphia / Kansas City / Oakland Athletics played in 14 World Series and won 9.
The Boston Red Sox played in 12 World Series and won 8, including the first World Series.
The St. Louis Cardinals appeared in 19 World Series in the National League and won 11.
The New York / San Francisco Giants played in 20 World Series and won 8.
The Brooklyn / Los Angeles Dodgers appeared in 19 World Series and won 6 (one copy of the note says 18 appearances).
The Cincinnati Reds appeared in 9 World Series and won 5.
American League teams have won 65 of the 113 World Series played (57.5%).
The New York Yankees' 27 titles account for 23.9% of all series played and 41.5% of American League wins.
The St. Louis Cardinals' 11 titles account for 9.7% of all series played and 23% of the 48 National League victories.
The World Series was first played in 1903 and most recently played in 2017.
The Houston Astros are the current champions, winning the 2017 World Series for their first title.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are the current runners-up.
The New York Yankees hold the most World Series titles, with 27.
The Commissioner's Trophy is awarded to the team that wins the World Series.
